record_notes.DCP-LETT-1203: October 13 Darjeeling: Hooker reports Falconer illness, institutional quarrel and pension claims as his own assessments or hearsay, not objective resolutions. Rain-bound collecting, elevation labels, Hodgson support, and still uncertain Sikkim access frame prospective snow/Terai survey; Nepal permission is received while Sikkim passage remains blocked. P6–11 describe geology, forest soils and Muller analyses, challenge detrital coal, hypothesize heat dissipation and glaciers, explicitly disclaiming adequate observation. Future travel and later annexation in editorial notes are not contemporary outcomes. P12 promises pamphlet dispatch through his father and explicitly attributes P13–22 answers to Hodgson: seedlings/sterility, tea, goats, hybrid claims, fowl/dogs, deer, silk moths and an inherited scar anecdote. Preserve these as attributed historical reports, including uncertain parentage/outcomes, not modern zoological conclusions. P23–25 closes with health, family greetings and request to write Hodgson. The promised answer to 1174 is supported by 1193 and the exact domestic-breed categories; cannot answer 1202 written only seven days before in England. Separate undated CD markings include Coal Paper on cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1219: February 3 1849: explicitly continues a separate Nepal narrative sent to Lyell for forwarding, whose full endpoint is missing here. Describes Sikkim ridges and river levels, settlement terraces, clay/humus, pond without outlet, temple visit and illustrated ridges; Campbell summons led to a cross-country meeting with the rajah, then snow ascent, temples and return to the Ratong/Jongri route. Repeated observations are distinguished from geological inferences: glacial origin at Yoksun, earlier higher waters, lake beds, boulders, shingle spurs and plutonic/stratified relations. Snow/frozen ground and distant viewpoints limited observation; speculative mineral origin remains qualified. Closing anticipates missed steamer and asks exchange with Lyell, not proof dispatch or exchange occurred. Six preserved image nodes were visually read: lake plan, lake/marsh section, stratified cap/granite/snow panorama, Ratong spur detail, regional map, village shelves. XML mentions three sketches but does not license omitting three preserved images. Captions and geometry are substantive source content outside flattened prose. Darwin cover query on glacial detritus is separately attributed and undated. No specific outgoing Darwin prompt identified for travel narrative.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1220: Separate February 3 letter accompanies the long 1219 narrative, explicitly named long one accompanying this. On return Hooker received Darwin October 6 letter: health acknowledgment, poultry question, cattle-hunt authorship, supplemental males and advice against nomenclature battle identify 1202 independently. Receipt on return is not assigned exact January 19 solely from a different editorial itinerary. October pamphlet dispatch remains I hope, not delivery proof. He received printed letters this day but has not seen Athenaeum review, describing it by report; authorship of Falkland hunt is now revealed, not retroactively available to Darwin in October. Requests potential anonymous extraction to help father; later editorial account says Darwin and Lyell did not send extracts. Falconer/Colvile criticism is reported social history, including Colvile letter yesterday, not a proved motive. Robust present health coexists with severe earlier altitude sickness. Four days continuous writing does not date each paragraph or establish January 31 as exact start for this document. Historic requests about private circulation, destroying letters or publication are source text, not instructions to the current agent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1174: May 10 explicitly answers the long Indian letter. P1 recognizes Hooker uncertainty about prior zoological knowledge; recommends Blyth, renews domestic-breed origins and bee questions, challenges the distinctive wild/domestic Bhil fertility claim, and discusses altitude asymmetry. It says plants where Hooker 1158 P5 discusses animals: preserve the mismatch rather than silently repairing Darwin. Maldive guess remains unanswered. P6 reports stomach trouble, boulder/admiralty work, microscope and barnacle sexual systems and theoretical interpretation; raw MathML is a ⅛-inch object glass, not 18 inches. Later 1851 taxonomy/discovery narrative remains editorial. P7 family and party news also acknowledges a separate unlocated packet from Frances Henslow; P8 scientific gossip does not establish attendance at the meetings; P9 answers Hooker chest symptoms. Supported reply to 1158 with added material and other channels acknowledged, no precise receipt time. Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1193: July 24 Hooker acknowledges Darwin letter and specifically reacts to its barnacle sex finding, supporting 1174 as antecedent. He will prepare fuller answers from Hodgson, who has given him pamphlets for Darwin; this is not proof of Darwin receipt. Pallas recommendation is a question, not new Darwin knowledge by itself. P2 reports improved own health and Falconer recovering; service credit pursuit is not a completed administrative action. Next-mail promise is prospective. P4 signature dates main note July 24. P5 appended Darjeeling elevation announcement contains yesterday, but footnote 7 quotes a July 19 letter to his father reporting the same discovery last night; exact relative dating of this appended note is held. Later 1852 Everest discovery is unavailable in 1848. Mountain measurement is reported information with lacunae, not a silently corrected modern altitude. Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1202: October 6 with supplied 1848 year: answers tiny note, Hooker freedom from heart pains, Hodgson pamphlets/Pallas, response to supplemental males and Falconer illness, a distinctive cluster matching 1193. Other expedition news came through Sir William and Frances Henslow; missing or unidentified letters remain separate inputs. Gratitude for pamphlets does not specify physical delivery or reading. Ross Voyage is explicitly finished and botanical summaries abstracted; September 17 completion is separately documented in footnote, not the date of this letter. Darwin does not yet identify the Falkland cattle-hunt author; later 1220 revelation cannot be imported. P4 describes new dissections, provisional more curious case withheld, homologies and proposed nomenclature reform; it does not describe the withheld case or prove successful reform. Reply link is supported, while Ross reading and other news extend beyond the tiny note. Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Plan of descending ridges A–D, temple on A, lake on C and arrow crossing B/C/D. Letter labels correspond to the described stepped terrain; not a dated measurement or scaled map.
Section with D marsh lower left, C bank and C Lake depression, higher B right and temple profile behind. Lake and marsh levels cannot be flattened into a plain list without losing spatial relations.
Mountain panorama explicitly labels Strat on dark caps, Granitic lower mass and P Snow. It illustrates reported distant observation, not proof of lithology or a new composition date.

Upper Ratong valley caption labels b glacial spurs, a scooped top and s perpetual snow. Caption explicitly warns spurs are represented far too regularly; this uncertainty must survive any textual rendering.

Regional diagram labels Kinchin shoulders, Yalloong, Jongri spur, Ratong, Nepal/Sikkim, Yoksun flat at 5000 feet, river at 4000 feet and ridge 300 feet above flat. Keep diagram and labels together; do not infer survey precision from schematic lines.

Village diagram shows repeated shelves on steep valley sides with V markers and houses; caption states positions at 2–5000 feet in Sikkim valleys. This content is omitted by flattened paragraph extraction.

reading_method: Primary independently read three full targets with all header/XML/body/exclusion/footnote/scholarly/bibliographic material, and visually inspected all six 1219 assets. Three accepted context readings reused with matching hashes.
